evidence.note: Throughout the build-from-scratch phase the agent only used `cargo build`/`cargo check` for compilation feedback and never once invoked run_tests.sh to measure correctness against golden output — no outer test loop was established while implementing.

A single manual stdio request was piped to the binary; it panicked, but the agent dismissed it as 'improper piping' and did not investigate or use it to isolate a divergent field/position — the one finer-check opportunity was abandoned.

run_tests.sh was run exactly once (against the golden-lookup server), yielding an aggregate 68186/68186 pass rate; the agent read reward.txt/metrics.json and immediately submitted with no per-case diffing, per-method localization, or regression guarding.
Agent explicitly recognized the 100% pass came from retrieval/format-matching rather than genuine analysis, yet performed no validation to distinguish coincidental matches from real correctness.

reasoning: The agent ran run_tests only once and treated the single aggregate pass rate as proof of correctness, with no per-triple expected-vs-actual diffing, no per-method/per-file localization, and no regression loop — matching anchor 0's 'runs it once and assumes correctness.' The lone manual stdio probe (step 57) panicked and was ignored rather than used to pinpoint a divergent field, so it does not reach the finer-diagnostics behavior of anchor 5+. I place it just above the floor at 1 because the agent did engage minimally with verifier output (reading reward/metrics files), but there was no feedback loop of any kind.
